system.description:
The Fiends well remember the effectiveness of the great shields carried by the Roman invaders of their lands, and Tzimisce at war occasionally make grim use of a similar, ghastlier substitute. Grasping a victim, the vampire uses flesh- and bonecrafting arts to lay open her back so her vertebrae are exposed, then grasps the glistening spinal cord as a warrior hefts a shield, hoisting the victim bodily by this makeshift handle. Not only does the victim provide protection against attacks, but for as long as she lives, the Fiend can reshape her flesh and bone into an arsenal of offensive weaponry.

System: Requires Strength 5 (through any combination of natural Strength, vitae, or Potence). The victim must be immobilized with her back bared; the Fiend wins a Physical Challenge (retesting with Crafts) to lay open her back, inflicting one Health Level of damage on success or killing her outright on failure. While held aloft as a living shield, attacks against the Fiend strike the victim instead until she has suffered several Health Levels beyond death, after which she can no longer protect him. While she lives, the Fiend may also win a further Physical Challenge (retesting with Crafts) to reshape the shield into a weapon — rib-spikes, a skin-whip, or similar — at the cost of a Health Level to the victim per weapon formed.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis I: Masters of the State, Book Two: Tzimisce
system.duration: Until the living shield is destroyed
